title: 7 Best Airtable Admin Panel Builders in 2026
summary: Airtable's own admin panel manages your organization. An admin panel on your base manages your data. Seven tools for the second, and where each stops.
body_markdown:
"Airtable admin panel" means two things. Airtable's own Admin Panel, on Enterprise plans, is where IT manages users, workspaces and security settings for the organization. An admin panel on Airtable is something else: screens where a support team, contractors or clients work on the records in a base without being invited to it, without seeing every table, and without an Airtable seat each.


This article covers both briefly, and then seven tools for the second kind, with the point where each one stops.


## Airtable's own Admin Panel


On Enterprise Scale plans, Airtable's Admin Panel lets administrators manage users and groups, workspaces and bases, sharing restrictions, SSO and audit logs across the organization. It governs Airtable accounts; it does not create interfaces for people who are not Airtable users.


## What an admin panel on Airtable needs


- Read and write access to the base through the API, with changes visible in Airtable immediately.
- Views that show only certain tables, records and fields to each person.
- Forms with validation, plus linked-record lookups.
- Users who are not Airtable collaborators, so seat costs do not grow with the team.
- Headroom for Airtable's API rate limits and record limits.

## The builders


### 1. Jet Admin


Jet Admin connects to your Airtable base and builds an admin panel on it: tables with search and filters, record pages with linked records, forms with validation, approval steps and dashboards. You describe the admin and Jet generates the screens, then you refine them visually or with custom components and code. Jet reads and writes your base live, so your team keeps working in Airtable while others use the app.


People sign in to the app instead of being added to the base, and roles decide which tables, records and fields each person sees, which Airtable sharing cannot do at record level. When the base reaches Airtable's limits, you can connect PostgreSQL and keep the same screens. Granular permissions, SSO and audit logs are on the Business plan and above; unlimited users are on every plan, including Free.


**Where it stops:** it works within Airtable's API rate limits, so very high-traffic apps are better on a database.


### 2. Airtable Interfaces


Interfaces are Airtable's built-in way to create dashboards, record review screens and forms inside a base. For people who already collaborate in Airtable, they are the simplest option.


**Where it stops:** editors need Airtable seats, and access is controlled per interface rather than per record for most setups.


### 3. Softr


Softr builds portals and internal apps on Airtable from pre-made blocks, with user groups and visibility rules. For a simple client portal, it is one of the fastest options.


**Where it stops:** it is limited to what its blocks do. Custom components or business logic beyond a block are where it ends.


### 4. Noloco


Noloco builds internal tools and portals on Airtable with roles, workflows and record-level permissions.


**Where it stops:** it has fewer data sources than general-purpose builders and no free plan.


### 5. Glide


Glide builds polished, mobile-friendly apps on Airtable data quickly.


**Where it stops:** complex logic and fine-grained permissions become harder as apps grow, and pricing depends on usage.


### 6. Retool


Retool connects to Airtable, and developers build internal tools with components and JavaScript.


**Where it stops:** it is priced per user and developer-maintained.


### 7. Airtable forms and shared views


Airtable's native forms and read-only shared views let people submit or see data without an account.


**Where it stops:** shared views expose everything in the view to anyone with the link, and forms only create records.


## Which to use


- **Staff, contractors or clients need record-level access without Airtable seats:** Jet Admin.
- **Everyone already works in Airtable:** Airtable Interfaces.
- **You need a simple client portal quickly:** Softr.
- **You want a mobile-first app:** Glide.
- **Developers will build and maintain the tool:** Retool.
- **You manage Airtable users across the company:** Airtable's Enterprise Admin Panel.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the Airtable Admin Panel?


It is Airtable's organization administration console on Enterprise plans, for managing users, workspaces, sharing and security settings.


### Can I build an admin panel on Airtable for people without Airtable accounts?


Yes. Tools such as Jet Admin, Softr and Noloco connect to your base and let people sign in to an app instead of Airtable.


### Can I give record-level access to Airtable data?


Not reliably inside Airtable alone. An app built on the base can show each user only their own records.


## Start with who needs access


If everyone works in Airtable, Interfaces are enough. If the people who need the data should not be in the base,[connect Airtable to Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/integrations/airtable) and give them an app with exactly their access.
